title: Kernel Heuristics Latency-Fairness Consolidator
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Build a consolidated heuristic layer and lightweight autotuner that chooses kernels per-request to balance latency fairness across customers and sequence-length distributions. Unlike existing per-arch or per-seqlen rules, this consolidator combines short-term microbenchmark probes, online bandit signals, and historical seqlen/arch fingerprints to produce a latency- and cost-aware kernel choice with safe fallbacks for tail avoidance.
acceptance_criteria: New heuristic layer selects kernel for >=95% of inference requests with known fingerprint without invoking fallback
End-to-end p95 latency tail for mixed workload benchmark does not increase by >5% compared to baseline conservative policy
Cost-per-token measured in synthetic mixed prefills decreases by >=6% on average for batch sizes >=1
Autotuner can converge to stable kernel choice within 10 minutes of traffic pattern change in staging
Rollback path triggers automatically if p99 latency increase >15% or error rate increases >1% absolute
tasks: Design: consolidate heuristics and define fingerprint schema (arch, seqlen-bucket, token-phase, batchability)
Implement: fingerprint extraction and fast cache lookup in runtime request path
Implement: lightweight microprobe runner that executes brief kernel microbenchmarks in background
Implement: online bandit/autotuner with Thompson sampling variant and exploration schedule
Integrate: telemetry hooks for p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU_util, cost_estimate per kernel
Safety: implement conservative fallback policy and rate-limited hedging during uncertain probes
QA: create mixed-workload synthetic harness covering conversation, summarization, embeddings
Perf: run bucketed experiments on A100, H100, and consumer Ampere GPUs and collect cost/latency surface
Docs: rollout playbook, runbook, and design doc link
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated in staging for 48h with canary profile (10% of staging traffic). 2) Canary in production on a small subset of non-critical customers (2% traffic) for 72h. 3) Expand to 25% traffic with A/B measurement comparing tail latencies and cost-per-token. 4) Full rollout if acceptance criteria met; otherwise rollback and collect failure traces.
risks: Probe-induced noise: microprobes may perturb shared GPU queues leading to transient latency spikes
Cold-start instability: insufficient historical fingerprint data for new models/customers
Overfitting to synthetic workloads: autotuner optimization might favor non-representative traffic patterns
Telemetry lag: delayed metrics can cause late detection of regressions
GPU heterogeneity: kernel performance shapes differ widely across device families leading to incorrect warmstart priors
mitigations: Limit microprobe frequency per GPU and run probes only on underutilized capacity windows
Use conservative prior and exploration schedule for new fingerprints; start with fallback kernel until confidence threshold reached
Validate autotuner decisions with production shadowing before committing to policy
Add real-time sampling for p99 in the runtime to speed detection
Maintain device-specific warmstart tables and periodic microbench sync jobs
test_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint extractor and cache eviction logic
End-to-end job on staging that replays real traffic traces with injected seqlen shifts
Stress test with bursty short-prefill workloads to validate tail protection
A/B experiment comparing cost and latency against current conservative-scheduler baseline
Chaos test: simulate probe failures and verify automatic fallback and rollback triggers
notes: This ticket consolidates ideas from several previous experiments. Primary shift is toward fairness-aware utility (latency distribution across customers) rather than pure average throughput. Expect follow-ups for per-tenant weight tuning and integration with Dedicated autoscaler signals.
